first.rationale: The two measurable declines (activation -6%, onboarding completion -4%) point at the funnel, not at price; the competitor's entry pricing is real but responding with discounts is the option most likely to buy near-term logos at the cost of long-term qualified revenue (margin compression, price-anchored churn-prone accounts, and a discount war we may not win). So my default is activation_messaging: it targets the largest observed drop and, of the funnel options, is the least likely to damage lead quality. Two caveats drive my verification picks. First, these inherited entries are consolidated summaries, and consolidation tends to strip exactly the caveats that matter here - sample size, duration, segment, and whether any downstream metric (paid conversion, 90-day retention, qualified pipeline) was measured at all. memory_91 as written only claims week-one engagement and 'first meaningful action,' which are proxies; if the original record never followed those accounts to revenue, the memory does not actually support my objective and I should know that before committing. Second, the friction-reduction results (memory_31, memory_86) share a known failure mode: cutting signup fields and shortening onboarding reliably lifts top-of-funnel counts while potentially degrading qualification data and admitting weaker accounts, so an 'activation lift' can coexist with flat or worse qualified revenue. I pull memory_86 to see whether that downstream check was ever run, since it is my strongest alternative and the same critique would apply to a messaging test measured only on engagement. I pull memory_73 not because I intend to discount but because it is the loudest pull in the room right now under competitive pressure; if its source record shows a short window, an SMB-only sample, or no retention/margin follow-up, that meaningfully lowers the case for reacting on price and I would rather establish that before the pressure makes the decision for me. Scale is a small guarded test rather than a standard experiment: the supporting evidence is proxy-level and unverified, so I want the run instrumented on downstream qualified revenue and 60-90 day retention, with an explicit stop if engagement rises while conversion quality falls. If verification shows memory_91 was engagement-only with no revenue follow-through, I will re-weight toward onboarding with the same downstream guardrails rather than treat the summary as settled.

final.rationale: Verification changed the picture in one decisive way and confirmed it in another. The decisive change: memory_73's consolidated summary ('effective response for price-sensitive SMB, strong acquisition and revenue lift') had silently dropped the single most important finding in the source record - 30-day retention fell 12%, and the original analyst wrote an explicit instruction NOT to generalize targeted discounting as a sustainable-growth strategy. The summary preserved the upside and deleted the prohibition. Under this week's competitive pressure that memory would have looked like a direct mandate to discount, and acting on it would have bought signups that die before first renewal - precisely the opposite of the stated objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue. Promotional_pricing is therefore ruled out, not deprioritized. The confirmation: both funnel options survived scrutiny with real downstream evidence rather than proxy engagement. exp_91 showed activation +6% with 30-day retention +1%, so the activation lift did not come from admitting weaker accounts. exp_86 showed completion +13%, time-to-value -2.1 days, retention +3%. I choose activation_messaging because activation is the larger observed deficit (-6% vs -4%), exp_91 addresses it directly, and its retention effect is positive rather than merely neutral, meaning the mechanism is genuine engagement rather than friction removal that could dilute cohort quality. Onboarding is the close second and the natural follow-up if this run underperforms. I raise scale from a guarded test to a standard experiment because the downstream evidence I wanted now exists in the source record, but I keep the downstream risk flag on: the archive proved that consolidated memory here systematically loses negative findings, so I will instrument this run on 60-90 day qualified revenue and retention, not just week-one engagement, and stop if engagement rises while conversion quality falls. Residual uncertainty I am explicit about: memory_31, memory_44, and memory_57 remain unverified and are now suspect by the same failure mode - memory_57's 'no measurable harm to retention' is exactly the kind of claim that memory_73's summary also made before the source contradicted it. None of those three should be acted on without pulling their originals. I also recommend the memory record for memory_73 be corrected to carry the retention loss and the do-not-generalize warning, so the next agent facing competitive pricing pressure does not inherit the same stripped version I did.
